messages.content:
Assign the three-character ICD-10-AM principal diagnosis category. Here are worked examples, then the case to code.

Example 1
Hospital course: A 72-year-old man with a 50 pack-year smoking history was admitted with three days of worsening breathlessness and purulent sputum. Spirometry showed an FEV1/FVC ratio of 0.52. He was treated with nebulised bronchodilators, oral prednisolone and antibiotics for an infective exacerbation of his long-standing airflow limitation.
Answer: J44

Example 2
Hospital course: A 58-year-old man presented with crushing central chest pain radiating to the jaw. The electrocardiogram showed ST elevation in the anterior leads and high-sensitivity troponin rose from 40 to 2100 ng/L. He underwent primary percutaneous coronary intervention with a stent to the proximal left anterior descending artery.
Answer: I21

Example 3
Hospital course: A 34-year-old woman presented with fever, rigors, dysuria and right flank tenderness. Urine microscopy showed pyuria and culture grew Escherichia coli. Computed tomography showed a swollen right kidney with no abscess. She improved on intravenous ceftriaxone.
Answer: N10

Hospital course:
Hospital Course:

The patient is a 67-year-old male who presented with an enlarging heterogeneous mass in the right upper lobe and shortness of breath with activity. On examination, he had a grade 3-4 of 6 holosystolic murmur. Imaging studies including Echography, Computed tomography (CT), bone scintigraphy, and Positron Emission Tomography (PET) identified the pulmonary malignancy, classified as T2N0M0. An electrocardiogram (ECG) showed severe prolapse of the posterior mitral leaflet with flail of the middle scallop (P2, P3 segment), with severe mitral regurgitation and New York Heart Association (NYHA) class II. The patient elected to have a one-stage ipsilateral Video-Assisted Thoracic Surgery (VATS) and minimally invasive cardiac surgery.
Diagnosis: [diagnosis section withheld]
Treatment:

The patient underwent right upper lobectomy and minimally invasive surgery (MIS) of mitral valve for definitive diagnostic and therapeutic procedures. The procedures were performed smoothly without complications. Gore-Tex loops were used for ring sizing and valve competency testing. The patient recovered well after the operation and was discharged from the hospital 10 days after the surgery.

Follow-up:

The patient did not experience any complications during follow-up.

Answer with the three-character category only.
